 BY ADV SRI.LAL K.JOSEPH  THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 10.04.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 2025:KER:31240 MACA NO. 2930 OF 2016  3  JUDGMENT

The petitioners in O.P.(M.V.) No.235/2008 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Punalur, is the appellant herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal)

2. The O.P. was filed under under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, by the mother and wife of the deceased by name Steney Idicula, who died in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 26.10.2007.

According to them, on 26.10.2007, at about 11.15 p.m., while the deceased was travelling in a car, a lorry having reg.no.KL-41/5223 driven by Respondent No.2 in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the vehicle of the deceased and as a result of which he sustained serious injuries and he succumbed to the injuries, on the same day.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioners, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P.
was 2025:KER:31240 MACA NO. 2930 OF 2016 Rs.1,00,00,000/-.
4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimonies of PW1 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A15, X1 to X4.
6.

After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.33,53,144/- rounded to Rs.33,53,150/-
and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioners preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Ciniya.Y.Mathew vs K.J.Varghese on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195787435/
2
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

9. Heard Sri.Anchal C. Vijayan, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners/appellants, and Sri.Lal K.Joseph, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
2025:KER:31240 MACA NO. 2930 OF 2016 10.
The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioners is regarding the income of the deceased as fixed by the Tribunal.

According to him, the deceased was an MBA degree holder and he was HR Manager in Trident Hilton, Cochin, earning Rs.45,000/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.23,000/-.The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.
11.
In order to prove the income, the learned counsel has relied upon Exts.A14, X1, X2, X3 & X4.
As per Ext.A4 payslip his monthly salary during September 2007 was Rs.23,604/-.
Ext.X2 shows that during the year 2006-2007 he was given performance award of Rs.28,809/-.
Ext .X3 shows that his probation was confirmed w.e.f. 30.06.2007.

Ext.X4 is the notice received from Income Tax Department stating that his annual income during the financial year 2008-2009 was Rs.2,89,212/-,
that out of the TDS of Rs.36835.99 only Rs.21787 was deducted and there was a short deduction of Rs.15,050/-.

As argued by the learned counsel for the petitioner, from Ext.X4 it can be seen that the salary of the deceased from April 2007 to October 2025:KER:31240 MACA NO. 2930 OF 2016 2007 was Rs.2,89,212/-, for which the Income Tax Payable was Rs.36835.99/- rounded to Rs.36836/-.
So, his salary for a period of seven months less the income tax will come to Rs.2,52,396/- so his monthly salary less the income tax will come to Rs.36537/-.

Therefore, the notional income of the deceased is to be taken as Rs.36537/-.
12.
On the date of accident, the deceased was aged 27 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is liable to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 17, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.

In the above circumstances, the loss of dependency will come to Rs.69,56,544/-.
13. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.25000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of consortium and Rs.50000/- towards love and affection.
No amount was awarded on the head 'loss of estate'.

In the light of the decision in Pranay Sethi (supra), the appellants are entitled to 2025:KER:31240 MACA NO. 2930 OF 2016 get a consolidated sum of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses, and the dependents (parents, children and spouse)
are entitled to get a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium, with an increase of 10% in every three years.
Therefore, towards loss of estate and funeral expense they are entitled to get a sum of Rs.18,150/- each.

Towards loss of consortium, petitioners together are entitled to get a sum Ciniya.Y.Mathew vs K.J.Varghese on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195787435/
3 of Rs.96800/- (48,400 x 2).

The deceased died in this case on the date of the accident.
In the above circumstances, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, Rs.25000/- is awarded on the aforesaid head.

16. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and 2025:KER:31240 MACA NO. 2930 OF 2016 reasonable.
17.
